title: Evaluation admission refuses with registered_check_root_rebound when more than four settled checks belong to a retired root generation (cap on retired-check dispositions)
outcome:
Reported by Engram::Merger (TermAl mailbox 5cdad9a7 #550, 2026-11-23 03:48Z) on Engram item w-9fcb's prelanding evaluation.
- What happened: termal_evaluate_acceptance with a valid criterion map was refused at 03:43:51Z with HTTP 409 registered_check_root_rebound on test-b3fb7572-93fe-466b-bddc-51d1d520a847. Supplying that exact retired-check disposition gave the same refusal at about 03:44Z, this time on test-af15db52-5f23-4ddf-b644-bd9bad58aec8.
- Why: five received or settled checks are tied to the retired root generation 3547 (test-5138a6a5, test-af15db52, test-b3fb7572, test-b8a43aa2, test-ed12aafe), and the current named root is generation 4350. Request-scoped retired-check dispositions are capped at four, so the five cannot all be disposed, and no evaluator spawns.
- Effect: an item whose history holds more than four settled checks on a retired root cannot be evaluated at all through the disposition route.
- Workaround proposed by the author: run one recognised focused check in the current named root, then request the evaluator, keeping every historical record.
acceptance: An acceptance evaluation request for an item whose history holds more than four received or settled checks on a retired root generation can be admitted without discarding or rewriting any historical record, either by disposing all of them in one request or by a rule that does not require per-check disposition. A behaviour test covers five such checks.
When admission still refuses, the refusal names every blocking check and the action that admits the request.
